title: Audit Overlap Analysis — Certification Architecture Redundancy Assessment

duplicate_reviews.detail: Every certification session deploys 4-7 agents that independently re-audit the exact same ExplanationWrong fields (A/B/C/D per item) for the same 4 defect classes (DL-008, DL-026, DL-013, DL-010). In S318 alone: Agent M (EW Audit), Agent E (Learner Safety), Agent A (Quality Gate), and Agent D (Technical Accuracy) all examined EW fields on the same 40 items. In S809: Agent D/E (Explanation Integrity), Agent F (Quality Gate Audit), Agent J (Learner Safety), Agent P (Certification Board), Agent N (QA Board) — 5 separate bodies examining identical EW data on the same 38 seeds.
duplicate_reviews.estimated_waste_per_session: 4-6 redundant agent-spawns per session re-auditing fields already audited by companion agents in the same session. In a 28-agent session like S809, ~20% of agent capacity (5-6 agents) is duplicate EW checking.

duplicate_reviews.dimension: ExplanationCorrect (EC) quality audit (citation depth, standard references, business interpretation)
duplicate_reviews.detail: EC depth/citation is audited by Technical Review (correctness of content), EQS (explanation quality), UIQS (overall item quality scoring), and the COSO Citation Agent (framework attribution) — four separate analyses of the same text field for overlapping criteria. S810.1 Agent C's COSO citation map and Agent B's DL-026 gap matrix both independently scored EC quality on the same 38 items.

duplicate_reviews.dimension: Portfolio Impact Analysis (certified-count projection, Domain E delta, completion-model numbers)
duplicate_reviews.detail: S318 explicitly deployed TWO agents (O and Q) producing the identically named SESSION318_PORTFOLIO_IMPACT_ANALYSIS.json. In S809: Agent R (Portfolio Impact), Agent S (Completion Forecast), Agent Y (Readiness Board) all computed the same certified-count projections from the same raw data. S809.1 Agent I, S809.2 Agent I, and S810.1 Agent I all independently forecast Domain E completion.

duplicate_reviews.dimension: Technical Accuracy Review (stem correctness, answer-key verification, COSO/framework alignment)
duplicate_reviews.detail: Technical accuracy overlaps with Learner Safety on stem-correctness and feedback quality. Certification Board and QA Board independently re-review the same answer-key verification results. S809: Agent C (Technical Review — ALL 38 PASS), Agent J (Learner Safety), Agent P (Certification Board UNANIMOUS), Agent N (QA Board ALL_AGREE) — four bodies affirming the same finding. S318: Agent D (Technical Accuracy), Agent E (Learner Safety), Agent B (Governance Preservation) all independently re-derived CorrectChoice values on the same items.
duplicate_reviews.estimated_waste_per_session: 4 agents redundantly verifying answer keys already confirmed by companion agents

duplicate_reviews.detail: S318: Agent A (Quality Gate — all 5 gates), Agent B (Governance Preservation — 27 checks including same gate dimensions), Agent F (Cross-Pack — structural integrity), Agent J/AA (Duplicate Prevention — Gate 0). 4 agents re-checking the same gates. S809: Agent F (Quality Gate — 6 gates), Agent AA (Duplicate Prevention — Gate 0), Agent O (Cross-Pack — same Gate 3 checks).
duplicate_reviews.estimated_waste_per_session: 3-4 agents redundantly verifying the same gate conditions

duplicate_reviews.dimension: Learner safety audit (misleading feedback, ambiguous stems, answer-key leakage, safety-gate)
duplicate_reviews.detail: Learner safety audits consume EW audit results (DL-008/026/010) and Technical Review conclusions. S809.1: Agent H (Safety Auditor) and S809: Agent J (Learner Safety) performed independent safety audits on the same 38 seeds and reached the same conclusions. S809.2 Agent G (Learner Safety Screen) re-audited the same 38 seeds again and found the same ZERO exposure result.
duplicate_reviews.estimated_waste_per_session: 2 agents performing safety audits that are trivially derivable from EW audit results

duplicate_reviews.dimension: Cross-Session Redundancy: 38 Domain E seeds audited 4 times (S809 → S809.1 → S809.2 → S810.1)
duplicate_reviews.detail: Four complete read-only sessions totaling ~56 agent-spawns examined the same 38 Domain E seeds (19 Pack C + 19 Pack D Section E) across overlapping dimensions without a single pack-file write. S809 found all 38 seeds blocked on Gate 2 (Explanation Quality). S809.1 then re-scoped the same 38 with 8 agents and found the same blockage. S809.2 then re-assessed readiness with 9 agents and found zero seeds certification-ready. S810.1 then produced a remediation blueprint with 11 agents. Between S809 and S809.2, a critical CC discrepancy was discovered (5/38 seeds have CorrectChoice disagreement between Agent C and D) that S809's 28 agents missed entirely — exposing that the larger session was not more thorough.
duplicate_reviews.estimated_waste_per_session: ~56 agent-spawns across 4 sessions on items that could have been scoped in 1 session. The S809 → S809.1 → S809.2 chain alone represents 45 agent-spawns (28+8+9) before any remediation blueprint existed. S810.1 added 11 more to produce the blueprint that S809.2 could have produced.

duplicate_reviews.dimension: Dashboard compilation (consolidated metrics from all agent outputs)
duplicate_reviews.detail: S318: Agent I produced SESSION318_DASHBOARD.json and Agent R also produced SESSION318_DASHBOARD.json — two agents writing to the same deliverable file. Additionally, the session summary itself (this markdown file) duplicates the dashboard's key metrics.
duplicate_reviews.estimated_waste_per_session: 1 redundant agent per session for dashboard/summary consolidation

duplicate_scans.scan_type: Governance guard test suite (27 checks, pre-flight + post-flight)
instances: Every session runs governance guard at pre-flight and post-flight. Multiple agents within a session also run it independently (S809: Agent V ran it; S810.1: Agent A ran it). The test suite takes seconds and produces identical results — pre+post is the required minimum per AGENTS.md §13. Additional intra-session runs by companion agents add no value.
duplicate_scans.note: Minor redundancy but acceptable given governance requirements. The 2x per session (pre + post) is required; 4-5x from multiple agents is not.

duplicate_reporting.metric: Domain E certified count (e.g., '228 Domain E Certified')
EW integrity metrics (DL-008/026/013 counts, empty-slot tallies)

shared_dimensions: ExplanationCorrect depth audit (both check for standard citations, formula inclusion, business interpretation)
ExplanationWrong non-empty verification (Technical checks correctness; EQS checks educational quality — same field, overlapping criteria)
COSO/framework citation accuracy (Technical verifies framework name is correct; EQS verifies it's present and explained)
Answer-key correctness (Technical verifies CC is right; EQS verifies EC explains why CC is right — both read the same CC+EC pair)
Technical_vs_EQS.detail: When Technical Review confirms an item has 'correct COSO terminology' and 'accurate answer key,' EQS re-reading the same ExplanationCorrect/ExplanationWrong fields to score 'explanation depth' is 60% redundant — the technical correctness already confirms the framework citation is appropriate.

shared_dimensions: ExplanationWrong per-slot analysis (both boards read and score every EW slot)
Distractor explanation quality (EQS checks clarity/completeness; DQS checks trap-engineering/specificity — overlapping criteria on the same text)
DL-013 boilerplate detection (both boards flag template text)
Choice-specificity verification (both check EW text addresses its specific distractor)
EQS_vs_DQS.detail: EQS and DQS are the most heavily overlapping boards. DQS is essentially a specialized subset of EQS focused on distractor engineering. In practice, both read every ExplanationWrong[A-D] field. An item that passes DQS at 90+ is almost guaranteed to pass EQS for the distractor dimension. These could be merged into a single 'Explanation Quality Board' with a distractor-engineering sub-score.

shared_dimensions: Distractor quality scoring (DQS produces a score; UIQS consumes it as a dimension input)
Overall item quality evaluation (UIQS aggregates DQS + EQS + other board scores)
DQS_vs_UIQS.detail: DQS→UIQS is a proper hierarchical relationship (board feeds into composite score). However, UIQS re-validates DQS inputs rather than trusting them, creating a secondary review layer. This is partially by design (CAQS §2 composite scoring) but the per-item re-scoring rather than aggregate-validation is inefficient.

shared_dimensions: Stem-answer consistency check (both verify the question has one defensible answer)
Feedback-correctness verification (both check EW fields for misleading content)
DL-008/DL-026 structural compliance (both verify CC-slot is empty, distractor slots are filled)
Technical_vs_Learner_Safety.detail: S318 exhibits this overlap clearly: Agent D (Technical Accuracy) and Agent E (Learner Safety) produced nearly identical DL-008/DL-026 findings on the same 40 items. The Learner Safety audit is ~50% a restatement of the Technical Accuracy audit filtered through a safety lens.

shared_dimensions: DL-008 compliance verification (same check, different framing)
Governance_Preservation_vs_Quality_Gate.detail: S318: Agent A (Quality Gate Verification — 5 gates) and Agent B (Governance Preservation Audit — 27 checks) overlapped on at least 3 gate dimensions (DL-008, DL-026, certified count stability). The governance audit adds depth (answer-key attestation, hash checks) but the gate-level overlap is substantial.

board_overlap_matrix.Board_Rationalization_Recommendation: Collapse from 6 boards (Technical, EQS, DQS, BQS, ExQS, UIQS) plus 3 governance bodies (Quality Gate, Governance Preservation, Learner Safety) to 4: (1) Technical & Safety Board (merging Technical Accuracy + Learner Safety), (2) Explanation Quality Board (merging EQS + DQS with a distractor sub-score), (3) Blueprint & Calibration Board (merging BQS + ExQS + difficulty/CL alignment), (4) Certification Governance Board (merging Quality Gate + Governance Preservation). UIQS becomes a composite scoring function, not a separate review board.

most_egregious_chain.scope: 38 Domain E seeds (19 Pack C + 19 Pack D Section E)
most_egregious_chain.detail: Four complete sessions examining the same 38 items without making a single pack-file modification. S809 (28 agents, 11 files, 0 writes). S809.1 (8 agents, 9 files, 0 writes). S809.2 (9 agents, 10 files, 0 writes). S810.1 (11 agents, 9 files, 0 writes). All four sessions confirmed the same core finding: '38 seeds need EW authoring before certification.' The CC discrepancy across 5 seeds (discovered in S809.2 and confirmed in S810.1) was missed entirely by S809's 28-agent deployment — a larger agent count did not produce more thorough results.

dimensions_reaudited_identically: DL-008: 38/38 clean in all 4 sessions — zero variance
DL-026: 53 empty slots confirmed in all 4 sessions — identical count
DL-013: 8-9 boilerplate slots in all 4 sessions — identical items flagged
Certified count: 2,221 in all 4 sessions — zero drift
Technical accuracy: ALL 38 PASS in all sessions that checked it — zero variance
items_reaudited_without_change.note: The only new finding that emerged across sessions was the CC discrepancy (5 seeds with Agent C vs Agent D mismatch), discovered in S809.2. This could have been found in S809 with proper within-object extraction methodology.

cross_session_redundancy.pattern: Pre-remediation session chains follow a predictable cycle: (1) Large multi-agent audit session establishes baseline defects, (2) Scoping session re-audits same items for 'readiness,' (3) Intelligence/blueprint session re-audits same items for 'remediation planning,' (4) Handoff session compiles all prior outputs into a batch plan. Sessions 2-4 could be collapsed into the initial audit session's post-processing step.

dimensions_shared: DL-008/DL-026/DL-013 structural compliance (both governance and content audits scan for these)
Certified-count denominator (both governance and content audits verify this)
Explanation field presence/completeness (both verify EW fields exist and are non-empty where required)
Answer-key integrity (governance checks for unauthorized changes; content checks for correctness — same CC field, different lens)
Pack-file structural integrity (governance checks hashes; content audits check parse-ability — same underlying concern)
governance_vs_content_overlap.detail: The Governance Preservation Audit (e.g., S318 Agent B) and the Quality Gate Verification (Agent A) both check DL-008, DL-026, and certified-count stability — the same structural dimensions that the Technical Accuracy, EW Integrity, and Learner Safety content audits check. The distinction between 'governance' and 'content' auditing has blurred: governance audits now contain content-dimension checks and content audits now include governance compliance checks. In S318, 27/27 governance guard checks included DL-008 (6 checks), DL-026 (5 checks), DL-013 (4 checks), and Blueprint Alignment (3 checks) — all content-quality dimensions.
governance_vs_content_overlap.recommendation: Formalize a single 'Certification Gate Audit' that produces both the governance attestation AND the content-quality report in one pass. The governance guard should focus on process integrity (hash stability, answer-key change detection, session isolation) while content-quality boards focus on item-level quality. Currently they are intertwingled.

summary: The certification architecture exhibits systematic redundancy across three axes: (1) Within-session: 4-7 agents per session independently re-audit the same ExplanationWrong fields for overlapping defect classes (DL-008/026/013/010), producing identical findings in 95%+ of cases. (2) Cross-session: 4 sessions (S809→S809.1→S809.2→S810.1) examined the same 38 Domain E seeds across ~56 agent-spawns with zero pack-file writes, all converging on the same finding ('needs EW authoring'). (3) Board-level: 6 quality boards (Technical, EQS, DQS, BQS, ExQS, UIQS) plus 3 governance bodies share overlapping dimensions — most critically EQS and DQS at ~70% overlap on ExplanationWrong evaluation. Each certification session produces 7-17 deliverables where 5 core metrics (certified count, Domain E count, EW integrity, UIQS score, governance guard status) are reported redundantly across 4-7 files. Recommended consolidation: merge 6 boards into 4, collapse multi-session read-only chains into single-session audit+plan, and reduce per-session agent count by ~40% by eliminating within-session duplicate reviews (EW audit, Technical+Safety, Portfolio Impact+Forecast).
